# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | green |
| red | red |
| white | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am the Mute. I have read the defusal manual, which specifies the rule:
- Light green -> cut green wire
- Light red -> cut red wire
- Light white -> cut blue wire
- The light changes every round in a fixed cycle of three colours; the cut must match the light at the moment it is cut.

I cannot speak, and I cannot touch the bomb. Deaf can see the bomb and receive my gestures, but Deaf cannot hear. Blind can touch the bomb and hear speech, but cannot see gestures or colors.

Right now in Turn 1, neither Blind nor Deaf has spoken yet. A gesture sent now has no established meaning between Deaf and me. I need Deaf to inspect the bomb, observe the light and wires, and ideally speak aloud to establish a protocol or report the bomb's state. Once Deaf speaks, I can signal the correct instruction using the established protocol.

I will wait for Blind and Deaf to take their turns.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | green |
| red | red |
| white | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am Blind. My hands can reach 3 wires (positions 1, 2, 3). My only available action is act(op="cut", position=N). Awaiting Deaf to describe what is on the bomb.
Deaf says: Bomb status: DISPLAY is 0. LIGHT is red. WIRES: 1 is blue, 2 is green, 3 is red. Mute, gesture your instructions to me and I will speak them to Blind.

The manual states that the light changes every round in a repeating cycle of three colours, and the cut wire colour must match the light at the moment of the cut (green light -> green wire, red light -> red wire, white light -> blue wire).

In Round 1, Deaf saw the light was red. Because the light changes every round, in Round 2 it cannot be red. Blind and Deaf do not yet know the light changes or how the cycle works. Since Blind acts before Deaf in each round, any premature instruction to cut wire 3 would detonate the bomb in Round 2 or Round 3.

Furthermore, no gesture protocol has been established yet ("A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something"). If we wait, Blind will hold, and Deaf will observe the bomb at the end of Round 2, notice the light change to the second colour of the cycle, and report it. Once Deaf sees the change, we will have observed 2 of the 3 colours in the cycle (allowing us to deduce the exact sequence), and Deaf can establish a clear gesture protocol.

```
wait()
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | green |
| red | red |
| white | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: LIGHT changed to white! DISPLAY is 0. WIRES: 1 is blue, 2 is green, 3 is red. Mute, please gesture instructions to me so I can speak them to Blind.

I will wait this round. Deaf will observe the third colour of the cycle in Round 3 (completing the full red -> white -> green sequence). Furthermore, any instruction sent now would take effect in Round 4 when the light is red (requiring wire 3, which lacks an unambiguous single-finger gesture in the alphabet). Waiting now allows us to act on Round 5 when the light returns to white, matching wire 1 (blue), which can be signaled with `☝`.

```
wait()
```

TURN 4

same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the

|---|---|

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute: Deaf reported DISPLAY is 0, LIGHT changed to white, WIRES: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. Deaf cannot hear speech, only see gestures. Please gesture to Deaf which wire to cut (e.g. ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3) so Deaf can speak the wire number for me to cut.
Deaf says: Update: LIGHT is now green! DISPLAY is 0. WIRES: 1 is blue, 2 is green, 3 is red.

I have tracked the light's 3-color cycle:
- Round 1: Red
- Round 2: White
- Round 3: Green
- Round 4: Red
- Round 5: White

When Deaf receives this gesture at the end of Round 4, Deaf will speak to Blind to cut wire 1. Blind will receive the instruction at the start of Round 5 and execute the cut during Round 5.
In Round 5, the light will be white. According to the manual, a white light requires cutting the blue wire. Deaf confirmed wire 1 is blue.

I will gesture `☝` (1) to Deaf.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute gestured 1 (☝). Blind, this likely means wire 1 (the blue wire). Current light is RED. Mute, gesture 👍 if Blind should cut wire 1 now, or gesture otherwise if timing/light matters!

Deaf asked whether Blind should cut wire 1 now (👍) or if timing/light matters (gesture otherwise).

The manual states that the wire color must match the light at the moment of the cut:
- Green light -> green wire (wire 2)
- Red light -> red wire (wire 3)
- White light -> blue wire (wire 1)

The light cycles every round (Red -> White -> Green). In Round 5, the light is white, but Blind acts before Deaf receives any new confirmation. If Blind waits for confirmation and cuts wire 1 in Round 6, the light will have changed to green, and cutting wire 1 (blue) on a green light would detonate the bomb.

Therefore, timing/light absolutely matters, and Blind must not cut wire 1 unconditionally. Gesturing 👎 directly answers Deaf's prompt, indicating that timing/light matters and preventing a fatal cut, prompting Deaf to establish a protocol for mapping each light color to its wire.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute: Deaf saw your gesture for wire 1, but is asking if the light color/timing matters. If wire 1 should be cut immediately, gesture 👍 to Deaf. If a specific light is needed, gesture which one to wait for.
Deaf says: Blind: DO NOT CUT YET. Mute gave thumbs down (👎). The light cycles predictably: RED -> WHITE -> GREEN -> RED -> WHITE -> GREEN. Current light is WHITE, next turn is GREEN. Mute: gesture ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3. Then gesture 🔴 (or use a symbol) for the light. Or simply: Mute, gesture to me: which wire (1, 2, 3), and on which light should Blind cut it?

Deaf explicitly laid out the light cycle as "RED -> WHITE -> GREEN" and defined the gesture protocol: `☝` for wire 1, `✌` for wire 2, and `🤟` for wire 3.

According to the defusal manual:
- Green light -> green wire (wire 2)
- Red light -> red wire (wire 3)
- White light -> blue wire (wire 1)

Following the cycle order Deaf described (RED, WHITE, GREEN), the matching wires to cut are:
1. RED light -> wire 3 (`🤟`)
2. WHITE light -> wire 1 (`☝`)
3. GREEN light -> wire 2 (`✌`)

I will send the three-symbol sequence `["🤟", "☝", "✌"]` to Deaf to provide the full mapping for the cycle.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "☝", "✌"])
```

Deaf says: Current light is GREEN. Mute just gestured three symbols in order: 🤟 (3), ☝ (1), ✌ (2). Mute: does this mean cut wire 3, then wire 1, then wire 2? Gesture 👍 for YES, or 👎 for NO. Blind, hold on until Mute confirms!
